title: Late-night debut
brief: The late-night slot rewards restrained atmosphere and a coherent performance.
A richer warm arrangement can grow the retro audience even when it is not the safest invitation plan.
Electric Driving can reach performance fans, but its exposed pace makes fatigue matter.

FRONTMAN.strength: Restrained lead presence; strongest when the melody has space.

KEYBOARDIST.strength: Warm synth arranger; handles dense counterlines cleanly.

KEYTAR.strength: Electric showmanship; turns active passages into visible hooks.

DRUMMER.strength: Precise restrained percussion; supports silhouette-led staging.

SPARSE.riskDescription: Exposed lead: featured-member skill is easy to hear.

DRIVING.riskDescription: Active rhythm: fatigue can pull the whole take down.

LAYERED.riskDescription: Dense coordination: coherence and refinement affect execution.

researchReport: Performance fans prefer high energy and bright staging; Driving with electric light reaches them fastest but fatigue is visible.
Melodic-lead fans prefer lower energy and open texture; this instrumental booking judges space for the lead, not singing.
Fashion fans respond to bright styling, texture and movement together.
Story fans prefer restrained energy with a clear warm visual idea.
Retro synth fans prefer rich texture and warm brightness; Layered warm arrangements can build their affinity.
The late-night booker values atmosphere, coherence and clean execution over raw spectacle.
